extra.message: localAgenda builds a raw SQL query with $queryRawUnsafe, interpolating the workspace_timezone cookie value (user-controlled) and teamId directly into the SQL string. A crafted timezone cookie (e.g. 'UTC'); DROP TABLE ...) is injected into the AT TIME ZONE clauses. The reports.dailyDigest counterpart uses the parameterized $queryRaw, confirming this is unsafe.

slaPrintout interpolates the user-controlled 'preset' value (from the x-print-preset header) directly into a shell command executed via spawn('bash', ['-c', `report-print --preset=${preset} ...`], { shell: true }). The escalationPrintout counterpart validates the preset against an allowlist and uses shell:false, confirming this is a command injection.

repackageAttachmentForRecordsRequest derives readerFormat from the attachment's original filename extension (attacker-controlled at upload time) and interpolates it into a shell command via execAsync. cleanFileName does not strip shell metacharacters (;, &, $, backticks), so a filename extension can inject commands.

readCaseArchiveFile joins the user-controlled fileName directly into the filesystem path without basename sanitization, allowing traversal outside the ticket's case-archive folder. The readCaseArchiveFileForPortal counterpart sanitizes with basename(), confirming this path traversal.

appendCaseCorrespondenceNote writes to a path built by joining the user-controlled fileName without sanitization, allowing arbitrary file write outside the case-archive directory. The appendCaseCorrespondenceNoteForPortal counterpart uses basename().

getDraftReferenceFile joins the user-controlled fileName into the reference file path without basename sanitization, enabling path traversal. getPublishedReferenceFile resolves the path and verifies it stays within the article folder.

uploadArticleCoverImage writes the uploaded file using file.originalname directly in join(coverImageDir, file.originalname), allowing arbitrary file write via a crafted filename containing ../ sequences.

previewTriageFormula compiles the admin-supplied 'expression' field into an arbitrary JavaScript function via new Function. The expression is not restricted to a safe DSL, so an authenticated admin (or anyone exploiting another vuln) can execute arbitrary code on the server.

queryEmployeeDirectory concatenates the user-controlled employeeId directly into an LDAP filter string ((uid=${dto.employeeId})). The DirectoryClient.escape method exists but is not applied here (integrations.verifyGroupAccess uses it), allowing LDAP filter injection to alter the search.

reviewCaseArchiveDocuments interpolates the user-controlled docType into an XPath-shaped selector without escaping. The reviewCaseArchiveDocumentsForPortal counterpart wraps values in escapeXPathString, confirming this XPath injection (can alter the predicate structure, e.g. inject @confidential='true' to surface confidential documents).

renderTicketReceipt splices the unescaped 'note' query parameter and ticket.subject directly into HTML markup returned with Content-Type text/html. renderTicketStatusSummary escapes via escapeHtml(), confirming this reflected/stored XSS.

articleWidgetEmbed renders article.title and article.body directly into an HTML response without escaping. These fields are stored from article creation/import and can contain script, yielding stored XSS in the public widget-embed endpoint.

parseLegacyMacroExport extracts entities declared in an uploaded XML DOCTYPE and resolveEntityValue reads any SYSTEM entity whose value begins with file:// via readFileSync, disclosing arbitrary local files. The importLegacyMacros endpoint (kb.controller) accepts staff-supplied XML, enabling XXE-style local file disclosure.

applySharedAgendaView decodes a base64url config from the URL and Object.assign's it wholesale into a Prisma user.update for the caller's own record without field validation. An attacker can set role='support_admin' (or active, passwordHash, organizationId) to escalate privileges.

extra.message: reconcileContactFromCrm spreads the entire user-supplied webhook payload into the contact update ({ ...contact, ...payload }), allowing arbitrary field overwrite. The reconcileContactFromDirectorySync counterpart whitelists only name/phone/title.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: recordEscalationDecision redirects to the user-supplied dto.returnTo without validation. acknowledgeQueueHandoff restricts the destination to ALLOWED_QUEUE_RETURN_PATHS, confirming this open redirect.

resolveDigestRelayReport trusts the relay code using jwt.decode() without verifying its signature, so any authenticated caller can forge a relayCode naming any teamId and read that team's SLA digest. The resolveSecureDigestRelayReport counterpart uses verifyAsync with a secret, confirming the bypass.

partnerWidgetStatus reflects the request Origin back into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any site to make credentialed cross-origin requests. The verified endpoint restricts origins to EMBEDDABLE_WIDGET_ORIGINS.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Inputs

extra.message: createWorkspaceSession generates the session id from Date.now and Math.random() with only two base36 random characters, making the workspace-session id predictable. This id is trusted by WorkspaceSessionGuard to authenticate agents, allowing session prediction/hijacking.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: JWT access tokens are signed with process.env.JWT_SECRET ?? 'local-support-desk-secret'. If JWT_SECRET is not set in production, a publicly-known default secret is used, allowing attackers to forge tokens. The same fallback appears in jwt-auth.guard.ts:29.
Digest relay tokens are verified with process.env.DIGEST_RELAY_SECRET ?? 'local-support-desk-secret'. The hardcoded fallback secret lets attackers forge signed relay links when the env var is absent.

contractSealKey falls back to a hardcoded key 'contract-archive-key' when CONTRACT_SEAL_KEY is not set, so sealed 'contract' attachments are encrypted with a publicly-known key and can be decrypted by anyone.

previewArticleBroadcast compiles the staff-supplied templateContent as a Handlebars template. User-controlled templates allow server-side template injection (prototype access / arbitrary object traversal). The previewArticleAnnouncement counterpart uses a fixed template.

extra.message: provisionFieldTechnicianAccount hashes the password with a client-controlled hashStrength (validated only to 4-14), allowing a cost of 4 that is trivially crackable. The provisionPartnerTechnicianAccount counterpart fixes the cost at 12.

extra.message: issueCallbackVerificationCode generates the 6-digit identity-verification code with Math.random() (non-cryptographic), making it predictable. The issueEscalationBridgeCode counterpart uses crypto.randomInt, confirming this weakness.
